correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for every n≥1,m≥2,1≤k≤m−1. Each prefix base clique is K_m and each vertex has at most one interclique link. A symmetric k-regular row-relation with uniform diagonal omits k vertices per clique and prevents any selected–omitted link, proving the upper bound. For the lower bound, nonempty cliques select at least m−k; empty cliques force every adjacent quotient clique to select at least m−k+1 and cannot be adjacent. Each clique of the quotient graph then contains selections totaling at least m(m−k), even in the presence of one empty prefix. Summing yields equality. The verifier independently checks 16 graph adjacencies, 75 constructions, 12 link structures and 22 exact small-case minima across 198420 masks; finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Resolves a specifically stated, fresh, all-parameter conjecture for a canonical recursively defined graph family. The upper relation construction simultaneously handles odd/even k, and the quotient-clique discharging lower bound controls genuinely nonuniform candidate solutions including empty base cliques. The result settles infinitely many previously conjectural parameter combinations, not a routine special case or a minor numerical increment.
